title: What If You Stepped Into Space Without a Suit?
description:
A new what-if every day at 5:48 pm (Riyadh).

In the vacuum of space you would not explode or freeze solid right away. With no air pressure, the oxygen would be pulled out of your blood and you would black out in about 10 to 15 seconds. The water on your tongue would start to boil: in a 1966 NASA vacuum chamber accident, test subject Jim LeBlanc said his last memory was saliva bubbling on his tongue. He was brought back to pressure within seconds and recovered. Holding your breath would be the worst thing to do, because the air in your lungs would expand and could tear them, so you would have to breathe out.

Sources: NASA Ask an Astronomer / NASA Goddard "what happens to the human body in a vacuum" (consciousness about 15 seconds); NASA Johnson Space Center 1966 vacuum chamber incident (Jim LeBlanc).
Narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs) and the pictures and clips are AI-generated. This is a thought experiment.

Would you remember to breathe out? Answer in the comments.
